diagnostic_evidence.quote: the tangencial component of $v$ vanishes at the boundary
\int_{\partial\Omega} k\, \delta v \cdot n\, dS
together with the assumption that $\Omega$ has a boundary $\partial\Omega$ and $v$ vanishes at $\partial\Omega$.
divergence-free smooth vector fields taking values on $\Omega$ which are parallel to the boundary
points lying in the border of the square identified

issues.failure_explanation: The paper claims its boundary assumption is the minimal requirement for the divergence-theorem step. That assumption is that the tangential component of v vanishes. The boundary term actually produced, ∫ k δv·n dS, involves the normal component, so tangential vanishing does not make it zero. The assumption is therefore neither sufficient nor minimal. Elsewhere the paper uses full no-slip v=0 (problem formulation, space C, proof), and it describes the Lie algebra by tangency. Full no-slip is stronger than needed and inconsistent with inviscid flow. The simulations use a periodic, identified domain, contradicting the claim that the assumption is needed for simulations.

failure_location.quote: Our assumption is the minimal requirement to satisfy Stokes theorem in the proof of the main result as well as for numerical simulation purposes.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume v·n=0 on ∂Ω and use the same condition in C, so that δv·n=0 and the boundary term vanishes. Correct the statement about simulations.
issues.overall_effect: The boundary setting of Theorems 1-2 is inconsistent. Under the announced assumption, the proof of Theorem 1 leaves an unaccounted boundary term.
issues.title: Stated boundary assumption does not kill the boundary term and conflicts with the other boundary conditions used
issues.why_classification: A local change of boundary condition makes the proof step valid and preserves all stated results.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \varphi(\cdot, t)\in \hbox{Diff}_{\hbox{vol}}(\Omega)
divergence-free smooth vector fields taking values on $\Omega$ which are parallel to the boundary
\Big\langle (Tv\circ \varphi)^{T} \pi + \frac{\partial \pi}{\partial t} + \text{grad }V \circ \varphi, \delta \varphi \Big\rangle
\langle a\circ\varphi,b\rangle=\langle a,b\circ\varphi^{-1}\rangle

issues.failure_explanation: C requires φ_s(·,t) ∈ Diff_vol(Ω). Admissible variations are therefore δφ=u∘φ with u divergence-free and tangent to ∂Ω, not arbitrary fields. If ⟨W,u∘φ⟩=0 for all such u, one only gets W∘φ^{-1}=grad q for an unknown q. In particular ⟨grad V∘φ,u∘φ⟩=⟨grad V,u⟩=0, consistent with ∫V∘φ=∫V being constant on Diff_vol. So V is invisible to the variation. Concretely, (φ,v,π+(grad h)∘φ,k+h) is again critical, but it violates the stated π-equation by (grad dh/dt)∘φ. The pointwise costate equation is therefore not a necessary condition on C.

failure_location.quote: Thus, again by the fundamental theorem of calculus of variations, we conclude that

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Option 1: drop the requirement φ(·,t) ∈ Diff_vol(Ω) from C, so δφ is free and incompressibility is enforced by the multiplier k. The change of variables is used only at the critical point, where φ is volume preserving. Option 2: keep C and state the costate equation modulo an undetermined gradient, which is absorbed into p in Theorem 2.
issues.overall_effect: The costate equation of Theorem 1, including its V-term, is unproved and false for the stated space C. The derivation of Theorem 2 rests on it.
issues.title: Fundamental lemma applied to constrained variations of φ in Theorem 1
issues.why_classification: The statements can be kept only by changing the variational space and re-justifying that optima are critical points there. Otherwise the conclusion must be weakened. This is more than a local typo-level fix but needs no new architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \Big\langle (Tv\circ \varphi)^{T} \pi + \frac{\partial \pi}{\partial t} + \text{grad }V \circ \varphi, \delta \varphi \Big\rangle
+ \langle k\, \text{div}\, v + V\circ \varphi \rangle
\min_{v(\cdot)}\int_{0}^{T}\left(\frac{1}{2}\langle v,v\rangle+\int_{\Omega}V\circ\varphi\right)dt
Optimal solutions of the problem in Section \ref{Problem:section} must be critical values of the functional $\mathcal{J}$.

issues.failure_explanation: Setting the proof's displayed δφ-coefficient to zero gives ∂π/∂t = −(Tv∘φ)^Tπ − grad V∘φ, not +grad V∘φ. The stated sign does not follow from J as defined. The root is J itself: it has −½⟨v,v⟩ but +⟨V∘φ⟩, so it is the Pontryagin functional for the cost ½⟨v,v⟩ − ∫V∘φ. The claim that optima of the stated cost are critical points of J is therefore inconsistent. Two sign errors cancel in the final statement.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace +⟨V∘φ⟩ by −⟨V∘φ⟩ in J and correct the proof accordingly. The statements of Theorems 1 and 2 then stand.
issues.overall_effect: For J as defined, Theorems 1-2 would carry the opposite sign of V. The stated versions correspond to the intended cost but are not what the proof derives.
issues.title: Sign inconsistency between cost, action J and the derived costate equation
issues.why_classification: A local sign correction in J restores consistency without changing any stated result.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We consider $S\subset\Omega$ to be the regular zero level set
decays to zero at some positive level set far away from the obstacle
a circular obstacle located at a single point

issues.failure_explanation: V=τ/f with f=0 on S⊂Ω is not smooth, or even bounded, on Ω. Near S, V≈τ/(2r(ρ−r)), whose integral across S diverges logarithmically (+∞ outside, −∞ inside). Hence ∫_Ω V∘φ, the cost and J are undefined. V is also negative inside the sphere and never vanishes on any level set. The simulation potential is singular on a circle of radius 0.5 inside [0,4π]^2, not at a single point. The theorems assume smooth V and so do not apply to the advertised barrier.

failure_location.quote: The potential function $V$ is an artificial smooth (or at least $C^{2}$) potential function

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require V smooth on the closure of Ω. For example, remove a neighbourhood of the obstacle from Ω or use a bounded regularized barrier. Adjust the example and the simulation accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The concrete obstacle-avoidance potential and the simulated potential lie outside the setting of the main results, and the optimal control problem is ill-posed for them.
issues.title: Proposed barrier potential is singular on S inside Ω, contradicting the smoothness assumption and making the cost undefined
issues.why_classification: The advertised barrier form, blowing up on S inside the fluid domain, must be abandoned or the domain changed. This is a limited but real change of setting.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \frac{\partial v}{\partial t}+v\cdot\hbox{grad}\,v =-\hbox{grad}\,(p - V)
The pressure $p$ is determined by the divergence-free (volume-preserving) constraint $\hbox{div}\,v=0$.
\langle a\circ\varphi,b\rangle=\langle a,b\circ\varphi^{-1}\rangle
Each $\varphi\in\hbox{Diff}_{\hbox{vol}}(\Omega)$ is a map from $\Omega$ to $\Omega$
we show how the artificial potential can help the fluid avoid a circular obstacle
imposing an artificial potential in the fluid context is equivalent to generating a desired pressure

issues.failure_explanation: The paper claims the potential ensures that optimal trajectories avoid S and that it helps the fluid avoid the obstacle. Three facts refute this. (i) For volume-preserving φ, ∫_Ω V∘φ = ∫_Ω V is constant, so the minimizers of the control problem do not depend on V. (ii) In (mod:eulereq) V enters only through grad(p−V), with p fixed by div v=0. Setting p̃=p−V gives exactly Euler's equations, so velocities and particle paths equal those of the V-free flow. (iii) φ(·,t) is onto Ω⊃S, so some particles lie on S at every time. No avoidance property is derived anywhere.

failure_location.quote: such an optimal trajectory does not intersect $S$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must introduce a mechanism by which V affects the incompressible velocity field and prove that particle trajectories avoid S. Possible mechanisms are a non-gradient control, a cost not invariant under Diff_vol, or a domain excluding the obstacle.
issues.overall_effect: The central motivation, the abstract and the interpretation of the simulations (obstacle avoidance via V) are unsupported. The modified Euler equation is the ordinary Euler equation with a relabelled pressure.
issues.title: Claimed obstacle avoidance is unsupported: V is absorbed into the pressure and the fluid fills Ω
issues.why_classification: The advertised obstacle-avoidance guarantee does not survive in any comparable form, and a fix needs a different formulation.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: using as initial conditions the functions $u(x,y,0) = - \sin y \cos x$ and $v(x,y,0)= \sin y \cos x$
The color map shows the value of the discrete divergence at each point.

issues.failure_explanation: For the stated data, ∂u/∂x+∂v/∂y = sin x sin y + cos x cos y = cos(x−y) ≠ 0. The central-difference discrete divergence is (sin Δx/Δx)cos(x−y) ≠ 0. The simulation therefore starts from inadmissible, non-solenoidal data. The divergence in the computed field cannot be attributed to the discretization, as the text does.

failure_location.quote: even though we depart from divergence-free initial conditions

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use divergence-free initial data, e.g. v(x,y,0)=sin x cos y (Taylor-Green), or project the initial data first, and rerun the simulation.
issues.overall_effect: The reported simulation does not start from an admissible state of (mod:eulereq), and the justification for the projection step rests on a false premise.
issues.title: Simulation initial data are not divergence-free, contrary to the stated premise
issues.why_classification: A local change of initial data and a rerun fix it, with no change to the theoretical results.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: we used finite differences to approximate the solution of the first equation in \eqref{mod:eulereq}
The pressure $p$ is determined by the divergence-free (volume-preserving) constraint $\hbox{div}\,v=0$.
due to incompressiblity of the fluid, the velocity field does not just 'flow out' from the obstacle
we present simulation results for the necessary conditions of optimality

issues.failure_explanation: The scheme specifies no way to compute p, and div v=0 is not enforced during the 140 steps. The intermediate dynamics are therefore compressible. The projection does not commute with the nonlinear advection, so projecting the final state once does not approximate the solution of (mod:eulereq); a pressure solve or projection is needed at every step. The displayed pattern comes from unconstrained dynamics, so attributing it to incompressibility is unsupported.

failure_location.quote: after the time integration stage is completed we projected our solution to a divergence free-vector field using the approach explained in the previous section

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Implement a projection (Chorin-type) method that applies the discrete Helmholtz projection, i.e. solves the pressure Poisson equation, at every time step, then redo the simulations.
issues.overall_effect: The figures do not represent solutions of the modified Euler equations or of the optimality conditions, so the numerical evidence is invalid.
issues.title: A single post-hoc Helmholtz projection does not integrate the incompressible modified Euler equation
issues.why_classification: It requires re-implementing the time integrator and rerunning all experiments, with possibly different conclusions, but uses a standard method.
